podcast.body: This song is highlighted as an example of The Velvet Underground's immersive sound. Played at a low volume, it creates an atmosphere conducive to sleep, while at extreme volume, its drone can alter one's mental and physical state. It showcases the band's ability to envelop listeners in sound and texture.

podcast.body: This song, described with the lyric "less girl child than a dark," exemplifies the sinister sound of The Velvet Underground, linking their early work to the dark aesthetics preceding goth music. "Shiny, shiny, shiny parts of the world. With less girl child than a dark."

podcast.body: This song is highlighted as exhibiting characteristics that would later define modern post-rock music, including non-traditional song structure, important texture, paramount atmospherics, and unusual subject matter. It used rock instruments in an unconventional way, lacking typical riffs, and was considered experimental and unsuitable for radio play at the time. "A couple of things about that song Venus and Furious. It has some of the characteristics that we would find in modern post rock music."
